service_at_issue: home health services after termination of coverage effective January 25, 2010
outcome_note: The Council upheld the termination because the beneficiary was not shown to be homebound despite attending adult day care four days a week and lacking a physician homebound determination.
facts: The appellant’s subsequent argument in support of the request is admitted into the record as Exh. MAC-2.

She requires monthly changes of her tracheotomy and periodic suctioning of the tracheotomy. The beneficiary has been living with her brother and his wife for the past five years. The appellant explains that about seven hours of home health nursing and aide assistance per week is needed to perform tracheotomy care, bathe the beneficiary daily, and assist with various other activities of daily living.

The record indicates that the beneficiary leaves home four days every week to engage in “sheltered workshop” activities (music therapy, games, puzzles, social skills development) at an adult day care center, sponsored by a county mental health/mental retardation program.

The record does not indicate specifically how many hours per day or each week the beneficiary spends engaging in adult day-care activities outside the home. But the appellant has testified that the beneficiary regularly leaves home four days every week to engage in such activities, and has done so for about two years.
